title: Routed experts split between the device and the CPU tier, in the device's bits
description: heterogeneous-expert-dispatch's partition. Host form: routes whose expert the expert_residency slot holds on the device run there (at most device_slots of them), the rest on the host; each route's weighted contribution is accepted into async-expert-contributions' ContributionGroup, which settles a token only when every route's receipt is done and sums them in route order, so the output is bitwise the reference whichever side ran a route. Device form on CUDA: nvfp4 / int4 experts; routes whose slot is -2 computed by host-expert-tier's CPU tier, posted and joined inside the stream through host-work-mailbox (one post and one join a layer, capturable), the others by the device part, summed in route order; both parts in host-expert-arithmetic's declared integer block order, so the split never changes a bit.

resident.description: forward() over the plugin's own store: the experts of each layer kept on the device (the lowest ids; -1 all); the others go to the CPU tier

max_tokens.description: the most tokens one post sends the CPU (a decode step or verify round; the mailbox holds this many tokens of the model's top routes); a longer call posts in pieces

join.description: how the stream waits for the CPU: auto takes the cheaper capturable join measured at load (host-work-mailbox measure_joins)

native.description: the CPU tier's rows: native (built at load) or the declared order in torch; without the native tier CPU routes are joined on the host, outside capture

workers.description: the CPU tier's worker threads (-1: one per physical core but the caller's)

pin.description: pin each CPU worker to a physical core of its own (Linux)

spin_us.description: the least an idle CPU worker spins before it sleeps

spin_max_us.description: an idle CPU worker spins as long as the recent gaps between batches (1.5 times the longest of the last 16), at most this, then sleeps: awake through a decode step's layers, asleep between steps (0: spin_us only). The default was measured on one machine (6 cores, WSL2, decode layers about 1.2 ms apart): measure your own cadence

rows_per_task.description: rows of one expert in a CPU pool task

idle_after_us.description: the mailbox's service thread polls the doorbells without pause this long after a job, then sleeps idle_sleep_us between polls: measured on one machine with decode layers about 1.2 ms apart

idle_sleep_us.description: the service thread's sleep between polls when idle (the first job after a pause waits up to this)
